questions.stem: A table lists eight blocks in the riverside district and six in the old town district, and eleven blocks lie in at least one of them. Using |A meet B| = |A| + |B| - |A union B|, how many blocks are in both?
questions.explanation: Rearranging the formula gives 8 + 6 - 11 = 3 blocks in both districts. A union of eleven means the overlap is counted twice in the two sizes, so three blocks must be shared.
questions.hint: Rearrange the counting formula for the overlap.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: explain what an intersection contains and what it leaves out
questions.stem: A club table has a swim column and a run column, and three students appear in both. Explain what the intersection of the two columns contains and what it leaves out.

answer.exemplar: The intersection of the swim and run columns contains exactly the three students who did both activities, because a set keeps only the elements that belong to every set being combined. It leaves out the students who swam only, the students who ran only, and every student who did neither, since those elements are missing from at least one of the two sets.

questions.explanation: An intersection keeps only the elements common to both sets, so it holds the three students in the swim and run columns. Swimmers who never ran, runners who never swam, and students doing neither are left out.
questions.hint: Keep the names found in both columns.

questions.stem: A parts table lists items shipped from the east warehouse and items shipped from the west warehouse. Explain what east minus west keeps and what it discards.

answer.exemplar: East minus west keeps every item that shipped from the east warehouse but not from the west, because set difference removes from the first set whatever the second set also contains. Items shipped from both warehouses are discarded, and items shipped only from the west never entered the first set, so they were never part of the difference to begin with.

questions.explanation: A difference keeps the first set's members that the second set lacks, so east only items survive. Items shipped from both warehouses are removed, and west only items were never in the first set.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Elements in exactly one of two sets
questions.learningObjective: compare exactly one with the union and the intersection
questions.stem: A sports table lists swimmers and runners, with two students in both sports. Explain how the exactly one set differs from the union and the intersection.

answer.exemplar: The exactly one set, sometimes called the symmetric difference, keeps the swimmers who do not run together with the runners who do not swim, so the two students in both sports appear nowhere in it. The union would keep every swimmer and every runner, including the two students in both, while the intersection would keep only those two students and nothing else.

questions.explanation: The exactly one set removes the shared students from both groups, so it holds swimmers only and runners only. The union keeps the shared students as well, and the intersection keeps nothing but them.
questions.hint: Compare which students the three sets keep.

questions.learningObjective: explain what a complement contains and how the universal set is chosen
questions.stem: A table lists every student in a school and a subset of them who take the elective. Explain what the complement of the elective list contains and how the universal set is chosen.

answer.exemplar: The complement of the elective list contains every student in the school who does not take the elective, because the complement is made of the members of the universal set that the elective set does not include. The universal set is the full school roster given in the table, and choosing a smaller set such as only the elective students would leave an empty complement that means nothing useful.

questions.explanation: A complement fills out the universal set, so it holds the school members who skip the elective. The universal set must be the full roster, since a smaller choice would produce a misleading complement.
questions.hint: Decide the universal set before the complement.
